sources.title: Gregory Ongie, Ajil Jalal, Christopher A. Metzler, Richard G. Baraniuk, Alexandros G. Dimakis, and Rebecca Willett, Deep Learning Techniques for Inverse Problems in Imaging, arXiv:2005.06001v1
sources.locator: Complete arXiv paper; §§3.1 and 4.1, PDF pp. 6–11, for matched training pairs, direct reconstruction maps and finite unrolled updates; §4.2.1, PDF pp. 11–13, for denoisers and learned generative priors.
sources.disposition: Read as a complete survey of learned inverse-imaging methods. It supports the distinctions in the definition; no convergence, stability or train-to-test guarantee is inferred.

contents.name: Matched-pair training and direct reconstruction maps
Finite unrolled updates, denoisers and learned generative priors

sources.title: Giannis Daras et al., A Survey on Diffusion Models for Inverse Problems, arXiv:2410.00083v1
sources.locator: Complete 38-page survey; §1.2 and §§2.4.2–2.4.3, PDF pp. 3 and 7–8, distinguish point reconstruction, score fields, conditional-score updates and posterior sampling; Appendix A.1, PDF p. 25, gives a finite-dimensional conditional-mean/MMSE proof.
sources.disposition: Read in full. Used as an independent method and finite-dimensional proof treatment; its scope is not extended to arbitrary sampler correctness or the Hilbert-target theorem.

contents.name: Point reconstruction, score fields, conditional-score updates and posterior sampling
Finite-dimensional conditional-mean/MMSE identity
contents.locator: Appendix A.1, PDF p. 25; context only, while the Hilbert-target result is proved locally.

sources.title: Masoumeh Dashti and Andrew M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems, arXiv:1302.6989v4
sources.locator: Complete 107-page lecture notes; §3.2, Theorem 3.4 and proof, for posterior kernels as data-indexed conditional laws; §4.1, Theorem 4.3 and proof, for posterior propriety and data-version hypotheses.
sources.disposition: Read in full, including both complete theorem proofs. Used for posterior-kernel context only; the local Hilbert-risk theorem assumes a probability kernel directly and does not import the source proof.

contents.name: Data-indexed posterior kernel and conditional-law formulation
Posterior propriety and data-version hypotheses
contents.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.3 and complete proof; context only, not used as the local Hilbert-risk proof.

sources.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory
sources.locator: Complete lecture notes; §5.3.1, Example 5.4, PDF pp. 104–105, gives scalar squared-error posterior risk as a quadratic in the action and identifies its posterior-mean minimizer when expectations exist.
sources.disposition: Read in full. It supplies an independent treatment of risk and the scalar posterior-mean calculation; the local Hilbert-target proof is complete and does not rely on this source as a substitute.

contents.name: Decision risk, Bayes risk, posterior risk and scalar squared-error minimizer
Scalar posterior risk quadratic under squared error
contents.locator: §5.3.1, Example 5.4, PDF pp. 104–105; coordinatewise Hilbert extension proved locally.

sources.title: Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems
sources.locator: Complete 13-page notes; §§4.1–4.2, PDF pp. 7–8, specify the parameter, action space, loss, measurable decision rule, and risk as expected loss under the observation law.
sources.disposition: Read in full as an independent statistical decision-theory treatment. The local risk definition keeps the joint train/test laws explicit and claims no comparison without a premise.

contents.name: Decision rules, loss and risk under the observation law

sources.title: Hongkai Zheng et al., InverseBench: Benchmarking Plug-and-Play Diffusion Priors for Inverse Problems in Physical Sciences, ICLR 2025
sources.locator: Complete official 29-page proceedings PDF; §5, PDF p. 10, and Appendix C, PDF pp. 28–29, report selected empirical behavior under out-of-distribution sources and prior mismatch.
sources.disposition: Fetched and inspected from the official ICLR proceedings after arXiv and OpenReview browser retrieval failed. Empirical findings are context only and supply no universal risk bound.

contents.name: Selected out-of-distribution and prior-mismatch benchmark results
contents.locator: §5, PDF p. 10; Appendix C, PDF pp. 28–29. Empirical observations only; no general risk theorem inferred.
